info.name: Money Lego: PayPal Sandbox end to end
info.description:
Every PayPal call Money Lego makes, both Channel3 calls, and the Money Lego API, in the order of an end-to-end demo.

**Setup**
1. Import `money-lego.postman_environment.json` and fill in the secrets (PayPal sandbox client id/secret, Channel3 key, Clerk session, webhook secret, cron secret).
2. Run *1. PayPal · Auth* first; the token is saved for every PayPal request.
3. Requests save the ids they create (order, capture, payout batch, invoice, product, workflow, run, approval node, share) for the next request, so run each folder top to bottom.

**Sandbox notes**
- Use sandbox personal accounts as buyers and payout recipients; a real address ends up `UNCLAIMED`.
- Payouts need a sandbox business account in a country that allows them (US works; India returns `PAYOUT_NOT_AVAILABLE`).
- Write requests send `PayPal-Request-Id`, as the app does, so a retry never creates a second object.

Source of truth: `server/paypal/api.ts`, `server/paypal/client.ts`, `server/integrations/channel3.ts`, `app/api/**`.

item.name: 1. PayPal · Auth
item.description: Client-credentials OAuth, as `server/paypal/client.ts` does it. The token is saved for every PayPal request below; its scopes show whether Payouts, Invoicing and Transaction Search are enabled for the app.

item.name: 2. PayPal · Checkout and capture
item.description: The hosted checkout path (`/pay/<key>`): create an order at the server's price, the buyer approves it, then capture. Open the saved `approve_url` in a browser and log in as a **sandbox personal account** before running *Capture order*.

exec: if (approve) { pm.collectionVariables.set('approve_url', approve.href); console.log('Open to approve:', approve.href); }

item.name: 3. PayPal · Checkout link (Channel3 sourcing)
item.description: What the *PayPal checkout link* block sends after you approve a Channel3 product: an order with a return URL, so the buyer pays from a link instead of the JS SDK buttons. The return URL lands on `/pay/done`; PayPal adds `token=<order id>`.

exec: pm.test('Has a payer-action link for the buyer', () => pm.expect(action).to.exist);
if (action) console.log('Send this to the buyer:', action.href);

item.name: Get checkout-link order (after the buyer pays)
4. PayPal · Payouts
item.description: What the *PayPal payout* and *Payout status* blocks call after an approval. Use a **sandbox personal account** email as `payout_receiver`; a real address ends up `UNCLAIMED` (`RECEIVER_UNREGISTERED`). Payouts need a sandbox app whose business account country allows them (a US business account works; India returns `PAYOUT_NOT_AVAILABLE`).

exec: console.log('batch', j.batch_header?.batch_status, '(accepted is not paid; check the batch next)');
pm.test('Item not unclaimed (use a sandbox account email)', () => pm.expect(item && item.transaction_status).to.not.eql('UNCLAIMED'));

item.name: 5. PayPal · Invoicing
item.description: The invoice blocks: *Create invoice* (draft), *Send invoice* (send or remind) and *Find invoices*. Send and remind are money-adjacent and sit behind an approval in Money Lego.

exec: const d = new Date(Date.now() + 14 * 864e5); pm.collectionVariables.set('due_date', d.toISOString().slice(0, 10));

item.name: 6. PayPal · Subscriptions and reporting
item.description: *Get subscription* (failed-payment recovery) and *Transactions* (weekly digest, ledger). Transaction Search must be enabled for the app, and new sandbox transactions can take a few hours to appear.

exec: const end = new Date(); const start = new Date(end - 7 * 864e5);

item.name: 7. PayPal · Webhooks
item.description: What `npm run paypal:webhook` does: register `{{app_url}}/api/integrations/paypal` for the events Money Lego handles (it must be a public HTTPS URL), and keep the list in sync. Money Lego verifies every delivery with *Verify webhook signature*.

request.description: Fill in the headers PayPal sent with a real delivery (paypal-transmission-id, -time, -sig, cert url, auth algo) and paste the exact event body as `webhook_event`.

item.name: 8. Channel3 · Products
item.description: The two Channel3 calls behind the *Channel3 product search* block, the AI pick, the post-approval price re-check and the run panel's Purchase card. Base `https://api.trychannel3.com`, key in `x-api-key`.

item.name: Search products (in stock, new, under budget)

exec: const offers = (j.offers || []).filter(o => o.availability === 'InStock').sort((a, b) => a.price.price - b.price.price);
console.log(j.title, '| cheapest in stock:', offers[0]?.price?.price, offers[0]?.price?.currency, offers[0]?.domain);

item.name: 9. Money Lego · Public checkout
item.description: The endpoints a buyer's browser uses, no sign-in. `checkout_key` is the part after `/pay/` on a workflow's checkout page (Editor → select the *PayPal checkout paid* trigger → Open). The workflow must be turned on.

item.name: Create checkout order (server sets the price)

item.name: Return page after a checkout link
10. Money Lego · Signed webhook trigger
item.description: Starts a workflow whose trigger is *Webhook trigger*. The body is signed with the workflow's signing secret (HMAC-SHA256, hex) in `x-money-lego-signature: sha256=<hex>`; the pre-request script signs it for you. `webhook_key` is the part after `/api/hooks/` in the trigger's settings. Repeating an `Idempotency-Key` never starts a second run.

item.name: 11. Money Lego · Signed-in API
item.description:
Everything the app does for a signed-in user. Sign in at `{{app_url}}` in a browser, then copy the `__session` cookie (DevTools → Application → Cookies) into the `clerk_session` variable. It expires after about a minute of inactivity; copy it again if you get 401.

Order for a demo: create from template → enable → start a run → read it (saves the waiting node) → approve → explain → payments.

request.description: The editor's autosave: `{ name, graph, expectedVersion }`. The pre-request script loads the workflow and resends its graph unchanged, so only the name changes. A stale `expectedVersion` returns STALE_WRITE.

exec: if (err || res.code !== 200) { console.error('Could not load the workflow', err || res.code); return; }
pm.request.body.update(JSON.stringify({ name: w.name.replace(/ \(Postman\)$/, '') + ' (Postman)', graph: w.graph, expectedVersion: w.version }, null, 2));

item.name: 12. Money Lego · Scheduler
item.description: The durable heartbeat a scheduler calls every minute: runs schedules, expires approvals, re-checks payouts and waiting checkouts. Bearer `CRON_SECRET`.

exec: // Every request: fail loudly on a server error and show Money Lego's error envelope.
try { const e = pm.response.json().error; if (e) console.warn(e.code, e.message, e.requestId || ''); } catch (_) {}
